standard_prerequisites: Flat pullback of cycles with relative dimension 0, and the definition of the k-dimensional part of a cycle, so that the pullback of a divisor by an etale morphism is defined
Deltas of points and their behaviour for etale morphisms, the generic point of an integral closed subspace and the scheme theoretic image construction for the induced closed subspace of the base
Henselizations of reduced Noetherian local rings, their total rings of fractions, and the length formula for the order of a rational function along an integral closed subspace of codimension 1
core_obligations: Show first that both sides are cycles: the map on underlying spaces is open, the irreducible components of X are locally finite, each component maps dominantly onto Y so that the restricted rational function is defined, and the sum is locally finite, while the left hand side is flat pullback with relative dimension 0
Compare dimensions: etale morphisms preserve the delta invariant, so every component of X has the same delta-dimension as Y and both sides are cycles of dimension one less

Reduce to a coefficient comparison at a generic point: for an integral closed subspace Z of X of the critical dimension, let Z' be its image in Y, let xi and xi' be the generic points, and work in the commutative square of henselizations of the local rings at xi and xi'

Handle the fact that the henselized local rings need not be domains by using their total rings of fractions, and express the coefficient of Z' in the divisor of g as a difference of lengths of the ring modulo the numerator and the denominator

Use that the coefficient of Z in the flat pullback of the divisor of g is that same integer, together with the flat and the surjective maps from the henselization at xi' to that at xi and then to that at xi restricted to the component, to reduce the claim to a length identity

Finish by computing the length over the base henselization as a sum of lengths over the quotients of the henselization at xi by its nonmaximal primes, and conclude because the index set is the disjoint union of the index sets of the components, each point of codimension zero lying on a unique component
proof_roadmap: Check that both sides are well defined cycles and that they have the same dimension
Pick an integral closed subspace of the critical dimension and set up the coefficient comparison at generic points in henselizations
Rewrite both coefficients as length differences over total rings of fractions and reduce to a length identity
Decompose the length over the base into lengths over the quotients by the nonmaximal primes and conclude by the disjoint union of the components
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the pullback formula for principal divisors along an etale morphism at source lines 1679-1690, label lemma-etale-pullback-principal-divisor, whose proof occupies source lines 1692-1803. The proof has two independent halves: a cycle-theoretic reduction that the two sides have the same dimension and that equality can be checked coefficient by coefficient at generic points, using the scheme theoretic image and the commutativity of henselization with the morphism, and a local computation of the coefficient as a difference of lengths over the total rings of fractions of henselized reduced local Noetherian rings, which are not assumed to be domains. The local half then needs the flat unramified ring map to equate lengths over base and total space, an additivity statement for lengths over the quotients by the nonmaximal primes, and the observation that the index set splits as the disjoint union over the components. The counted statement records neither the coefficient comparison nor the length identity.
